clue.text: Performing one's duty?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone carrying out an obligation they owe
setter's reading: for a performer, the duty is to carry on with the act whatever happens

explanation.surface: A question about simply getting on with what is expected of you.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SHOW MUST GO ON is the theatrical motto that a performance continues regardless of mishap; 'Performing' points to the stage rather than to duty in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage saying expresses the performer's obligation to carry on whatever goes wrong, which is exactly a performer's duty.

clue.text: Period with insects, when you're having fun … ?

blocks.note: time is a period
flies are insects

explanation.surface: A stretch of hours buzzing with bugs, a strange idea of a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the end of the saying 'time flies when you're having fun', which the answer completes.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says hours seem to pass quickly when people enjoy themselves, so the answer completes it.

clue.text: After work, retire to a foreign country

indicators.note: after being worked, the letters have been kneaded into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the job is over, someone moves abroad to enjoy their retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country on the Red Sea coast of north-east Africa, foreign to a British reader.

clue.text: Hot and stuffy, but not needing to shampoo

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a stuffy room is airless; and joins the two

explanation.surface: A sweaty, close day, but at least one bald person has no hair to wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bald has no hair to wash, so they have no need of shampoo.

clue.text: One won't get drunk on this

definitions.text: One won't get drunk on this

blocks.clueFragment: One won't get drunk on this
blocks.note: surface reading: a drink too weak to intoxicate
setter's reading: the idiom for abstaining, being on a horse-drawn vehicle

explanation.surface: A remark about some feeble beverage that cannot make anyone tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'on the wagon' is the idiom for having given up alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the wagon is teetotal, so they will not get drunk while there.

clue.text: Doctor's relaxed, glorious time

indicators.note: something relaxed has loosened its hold, so the letters are free to rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A physician enjoys a leisurely, wonderful break.
explanation.definitionFit: A urologist is a medical specialist in the urinary tract, a kind of physician.

clue.text: Be inclined to inhale gas? No more now!

indicators.note: inhaling draws something inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: to tend to do something is to be inclined to
He is the symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to breathe in some gas declares that it is all over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what appears when a story finishes, announcing there is nothing further to come.

clue.text: Heard dismissal of storyteller is a result needing explaining

indicators.note: heard means the clue words are spoken, and their sound is what counts

blocks.note: out is a batter's dismissal in cricket
a liar tells stories

explanation.surface: Getting a cricketer out turns out to be a statistical oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics an outlier is a data point far from the rest, which calls for an explanation.

clue.text: The naked President?

blocks.note: surface reading: a head of state with no clothes
setter's reading: with nothing on, where 'nix' is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about an unclothed head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the surname as NIX ON: nix is slang for nothing, so it reads as 'nothing on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Nixon was the thirty-seventh US President, who resigned after Watergate.

clue.text: Posting a little malicious? Sickening

indicators.note: only a little of the next word is wanted, so just its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of malicious
sickening in the sense of falling ill, ailing

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a slightly nasty letter they sent was in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Mailing and posting both mean sending something by the postal service, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: It's plain a kiss is to ask too much

blocks.note: overt means plain, open to view
taken as written
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A clear remark that requesting a kiss is asking for more than is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtax is to make excessive demands on someone, placing too great a burden on them.

clue.text: In endless rage, this flies?

indicators.note: something without its end loses its final letter

blocks.note: fury is violent rage

explanation.surface: When tempers run high, something is said to fly through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom that 'the fur flies' when people fight angrily, so the whole clue reads as a hint too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says the fur flies during a fierce quarrel, so fur is the thing that flies.

clue.text: Abe's pub where all want a good argument?

definitions.text: where all want a good argument?

blocks.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US President
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A tavern belonging to Abe where every drinker is spoiling for a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: LINCOLN'S INN is one of the four Inns of Court in London, to which barristers belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers of this Inn of Court earn their living by making persuasive legal arguments, cryptically hinted.

clue.text: Not here for the Latin translation

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who is absent
setter's reading: put the idea of being away into Latin legal phrasing

explanation.surface: A note that someone is missing, with an instruction to render it in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: IN ABSENTIA is the Latin phrase used, for example, when someone is tried or awarded a degree without being present.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means while absent, describing a person who is away from the proceedings.

clue.text: To be sent in storm around Yellow Sea causes queasiness

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters get thrown out of order
around means one part goes outside, enclosing the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Au is the symbol for gold, a yellow metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being dispatched through a gale on Chinese waters makes anyone seasick.
explanation.definitionFit: To nauseate is to make someone feel sick, so the verb means producing queasiness.

clue.text: One has a close relationship with a hooker

definitions.text: One has a close relationship with a hooker

blocks.clueFragment: One has a close relationship with a hooker
blocks.note: surface reading: someone intimately involved with a prostitute
setter's reading: the rugby hooker, flanked in the scrum by a forward binding tightly beside them

explanation.surface: A slightly scandalous remark about someone's intimate companion.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the hooker is the front-row player between the two props, who bind onto them in every scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop forward binds physically to the hooker in the scrum, a literally close relationship on the pitch.

clue.text: To shoot old fowl is work of little merit

blocks.note: to pot is to shoot game
a boiler is an old chicken fit only for stewing

explanation.surface: Bagging an elderly bird is a poor sort of achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book written quickly just for money, and so of low artistic quality.

clue.text: Guerrilla, one put in separate clinic

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the others

blocks.note: to part is to separate
I is the Roman numeral one
san is short for sanatorium, a clinic

explanation.surface: A fighter is admitted to an isolation ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an irregular armed force fighting an occupier, much the same as a guerrilla.

clue.text: Falstaff loved this bed

blocks.note: first meaning: the old Spanish white wine Shakespeare's Falstaff drinks constantly
second meaning: slang for a bed, as in hitting it

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's fat knight was fond of his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack was a fortified wine like sherry, Falstaff's favourite tipple in Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the sherry-like wine Falstaff praises and, informally, the bed one goes to sleep in.

clue.text: Coach – it slithered all over the place

indicators.note: slithering is sliding about, so the letters slip out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bus skids across an icy road in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chaotic is disordered and confused, which is the idiomatic sense of all over the place.

clue.text: Wipe garment, a novel sort of wrap

blocks.note: to dust is to wipe surfaces clean
a jacket is a garment

explanation.surface: Clean the clothing, which is an unusual kind of shawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new', but it is the book the jacket wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust jacket is the removable paper cover wrapped around a hardback book such as a novel.

clue.text: Summarily dismiss, giving one the boot?

blocks.note: first meaning: to expel someone abruptly
second meaning, playfully literal: striking out with a foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving one the boot' is itself an idiom for dismissal, but the question mark invites the literal kick.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to eject someone forcibly, and literally to strike outward with the foot.

clue.text: Pretend article comes from native healer

blocks.note: sham means pretend, fake
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fake newspaper piece was written by a tribal medicine man.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a spiritual figure in traditional societies believed to cure illness, a tribal medicine man.

clue.text: Fall asleep on hard wood in front of film: "On the Road" screening

blocks.note: to crash is informal for falling asleep
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
elm is a wood
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Dozing off on a wooden bench before a showing of the Kerouac adaptation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the Road' is set up as a film title, but it means on the road, and the screening is protection for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash helmet shields a rider's head while travelling on the road, so it is protective screening.

clue.text: One's fast in the water but slow on land

blocks.note: first meaning: the front swimming stroke, the quickest one
second meaning: moving slowly on hands and knees

explanation.walkthrough: The contrast between fast and slow hides that one word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Front crawl is the fastest swimming stroke, while to crawl on land is to move at a snail's pace.

clue.text: Precocious girl turns up without getting changed

indicators.note: in a down light turning up reads it bottom to top, and staying unchanged means it reads the same both ways

blocks.note: the answer itself is the fodder, read upwards

explanation.surface: A cheeky young miss comes in without bothering to dress up.
explanation.walkthrough: A little madam is a girl who behaves as if she were much older and grander.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a girl a little madam means she is bossy and acts older than her years, precocious.

clue.text: Call from pigeon cage, not quiet

indicators.note: not means the following letter is taken away from the word before it

blocks.note: a coop is a cage for birds
P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A sound from a pigeon cage that is anything but silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft murmuring sound a pigeon or dove makes is called its coo.

clue.text: Food dispenser placed on the floor of the car?

blocks.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a mat is something placed on the floor

explanation.surface: A snack machine that somebody put in the footwell of their vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: An automat is a coin-operated food machine, or a cafeteria made of them, mainly American.
explanation.definitionFit: An automat is a vending machine that hands out meals or snacks when coins are inserted.

clue.text: I sloped off to strip

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or awry, so the letters do not stay in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slinks away in order to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil a place is to plunder or strip it of its valuables.

clue.text: Scottish mystery the McLorens' sons resolved

indicators.note: resolved suggests something broken down and worked out again in a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Highland family's boys finally solve a riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed creature of the Scottish loch is a famous unsolved mystery, never proven to exist.
